summary: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture is Meta's own answer to phone scanning, done with a headset: a Quest 3 or 3S user walks a room, the images and headset poses go to Meta's servers, and a Gaussian splat replica comes back, taking up to eight hours to process. It is scored here with the other capture product on the same platform — the experimental Splat interface in Meta's Spatial development kit, which loads splats on the same headsets from SPZ files — because together they show Meta's position clearly: the consumer capture path is closed and the developer path is open to a format somebody else published. Hyperscape shed features in 2026 rather than gaining them. Sharing a capture, inviting people into it and being in one together were all withdrawn on 12 May 2026; the worlds moved out of Horizon Worlds and are now view-only in the capture application itself, rendered on the headset instead of streamed from a server, and the separate preview application is gone. There is no export of any kind, no format, no interface for programs and no documented developer route into a Hyperscape capture: what you scan stays inside Meta's product on the headset that scanned it. The rules around capture, on the other hand, are the most explicit of any subject in this lane — a minimum room size, no people or pets, permission for the space, a code of conduct, a reporting tool, and a plain statement that the images go to Meta and may be used to improve Meta's products.

coverage.note: Splats are drawn on the headset itself now, where they used to be rendered in a data centre and streamed. Nothing about the pipeline is published for the capture application; the development kit exposes a splat feature that has to be registered and opted into.
